docs.title: QuestMod
docs.text: QuestMod adds a classic-style quest system to Minecraft Forge 1.20.1: a Quest Master (NPC) that offers, takes in and rewards quests, with a clear panel instead of a giant tree, built to work with any mod.

docs.title: What it includes
docs.text:
• Several quest types: kill, break, consume, craft, smelt and deliver items. Objectives accept IDs from any mod and tags (#minecraft:logs).
  • Several objectives per quest, several rewards with NBT, experience and milestones with percentage rewards.
  • Requirements and chains of quests, sections (for example one per mod) and automation (auto-accept and auto-claim).
  • Community quests with a server-wide counter, where each player decides whether to take part.
  • Customizable NPCs: player skin, skin from a link, resource pack texture, the model of another mob from any mod, or an item with a 3D model.
  • Quest book (key or item) to use it without NPCs, and datapack quests for modpacks.
  • In-game editor with an item picker (inventory or the whole registry, mods included).
  • Customizable: colors and textures through resource packs, and translatable to any language.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
If you are... Read A player Getting started A server admin Getting started, Quests and NPCs A modpack author Modpacks and datapacks A resource pack designer Theming A translator Languages

Requirements

Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47.2.0 or newer, and Java 17. The mod must be installed on both the client and the server.

docs.title: With other mods
docs.text:
• IDs from any mod. Objectives accept mobs, blocks and items from any installed mod. The editor lists them (the picker's All tab) and warns in chat if the target doesn't exist on the server.
  • Tags. A tag like #forge:ores counts whatever any mod puts in it, with no setup.
  • Mobs and models from other mods on NPCs. The NPC is drawn with the mob's real renderer, so mods with their own models (for example GeckoLib) work too. If it fails, that client sees the default skin.
  • Items with 3D models. With CustomModelData and a resource pack.

docs.title: What counts and what doesn't
docs.text:
Type Counts Doesn't count kill Kills with weapons and projectiles/arrows fired by the player Killing players. What a FakePlayer does (turrets, deployers) break Breaking blocks as a player What machines from other mods break; breaking blocks a protection mod prevents eat Food and also drinks (potions, milk, mod drinks) What another creature consumes craft Crafting at a table or crafting menus Machines that don't use normal crafting smelt Taking the result out of a furnace What hoppers or other automation move deliver Delivering with the panel button Dropping items on the ground

Actions by fake players (FakePlayer: deployers, turrets, quarries) don't add progress. Kill and break events are counted with low priority: if a protection (claims) mod cancels the action, it doesn't count.

docs.title: Client and server
docs.text: The mod must be on both sides with the same version. Mods for the mobs, blocks or items you use in a quest must also be on both sides (otherwise the server or client won't recognize the ID).

docs.title: Existing worlds
docs.text: When updating, earlier quests and progress are migrated automatically. Old quests keep NPC only access, and existing NPCs keep offering all quests.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
I can't edit anything in my singleplayer world

In a singleplayer world the owner is an admin if singleplayerOwnerIsAdmin is true (the default). A modpack may have set it to false in defaultconfigs/questmod-server.toml. Change it in your world's serverconfig/questmod-server.toml, or enable cheats.

I can't see the quest book / the K key does nothing

Check bookEnabled and giveBook in the server config. Also, the book only shows quests with Book only or NPC and book access: an NPC only quest doesn't appear.

My quest doesn't advance
  • If the target doesn't exist on the server (a mod is missing or the ID/tag is misspelled), you got a warning in chat when saving and that objective won't advance.
  • You must have accepted the quest (in community quests, joined).
  • Actions by FakePlayers and anything a protection mod cancels don't count. See Compatibility.
The Accept or Claim button does nothing

With an NPC you must be within 10 blocks and that NPC must offer the quest (check its Quests tab). A Locked quest asks you to complete its requirements first.

A community quest doesn't add up

Only what you do after joining counts. Press Join in the panel.

An NPC shows the default skin

The mob's mod may not be on your client, the model may have failed, or link skins may be disabled (npc.allowUrlSkins). A player skin takes a moment to download.

My datapack quest doesn't show up

Check the log: invalid files are skipped and the reason is given. Run /reload after changing files and check the path data/<ns>/questmod/quests/. Datapack quests are read-only in game.

My theme textures aren't applied

Reload with F3 + T, check that the resource pack is active and that theme.json is in assets/questmod/. If an image is missing or the JSON is wrong, the log says so and the usual color is used.

How do I reset a player's progress?

/questmod reset <player> for everything, or /questmod reset <player> <quest> for one. To repeat a community quest for everyone: /questmod community reset <quest>.

What happens to my quests when updating?

They are migrated automatically. Old quests stay as NPC only, and existing NPCs keep offering everything. Update client and server at the same time.

docs.title: For players
docs.text:
• Opening quests: right-click a Quest Master, or use the K key / the Quest Book item if the server allows it.
  • The panel: the quest list is on the left and the details on the right. Tabs separate Available, In progress and Done. If there are sections, they appear as icons on the left.
  • Accept, deliver and claim: press Accept on an available quest. When you meet its objectives, Claim! appears and you get the rewards. Some quests ask you to Deliver items to the NPC. To accept, deliver or claim with an NPC you must be within 10 blocks of it.
  • HUD: accepted quests are shown on a side of the screen. Press G to expand each step separately.
  • Marker: above an NPC, a red ! means new quests and a gold one means rewards to claim.

Community quests

A community quest has a counter shared by the whole server. Press Join to take part: only what you do after joining counts.

docs.title: 1. Get an NPC
docs.text: Use the Quest Master egg (creative Tools tab) or /summon questmod:quest_npc.

docs.title: 2. Configure it
docs.text:
Shift + right-click the NPC (as an admin) opens its editor, with two tabs:

  • Appearance: name, skin, model of another mob or item, scale. See NPCs.
  • Quests: which quests it offers (all of them, or only the ones you pick).

docs.title: 3. Create a quest
docs.text:
Right-click the NPC and press + New quest. The editor has four pages:

  1. General: name, description, icon, section, where it is offered from, and type.
  2. Objectives: up to 6. Press the little box, pick a mob, block or item in the panel on the right, and set the amount.
  3. Requirements: quests that must be claimed first.
  4. Rewards: items, experience and milestones.

Press Save. If a mob or item doesn't exist on the server (for example a mod is missing), the quest is still saved but you get a warning in chat.

docs.title: Who is an admin?
docs.text: An operator with the configured level (2 by default) and, in a singleplayer world, also the world owner even without cheats. It can be changed in the server configuration.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Minecraft 1.20.1 with Forge 47.2.0 or newer.
  • Java 17.
  • The mod must be installed on the server and on every client. If the versions don't match, the client can't join (the mod checks a network protocol version).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Download the .jar from CurseForge.
  2. Copy it into the mods/ folder of the client and the server.
  3. Start the game. The configuration files are created.

docs.title: Configuration files
docs.text:
File Where What for config/questmod-client.toml Client HUD, skin downloads and the NPC ! marker serverconfig/questmod-server.toml Each world Who is an admin, the quest book and the welcome book defaultconfigs/questmod-server.toml Server or modpack Default server config values for new worlds

The options are described in the Reference.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
Key Action K Opens the quest book (no NPC needed) G Shows or hides each quest's steps in the HUD

They can be changed in Options → Controls → QuestMod.

docs.title: Updating from an earlier version
docs.text: Quests and progress from earlier versions are read without problems: progress is migrated automatically the first time a player joins. Because the network protocol changes between versions, update the mod on the server and on the clients at the same time.

docs.title: Languages
docs.text: All of the mod's texts (screens, server messages, items, keys) are translation keys in assets/questmod/lang/.

docs.title: Included languages
docs.text: English (en_us) and Spanish (es_mx, es_es, es_ar, es_cl, es_uy, es_ve). Each player sees the mod in their language even if the server is in another: server messages travel as keys and each client translates them. Languages without a translation fall back to English.

docs.title: Adding a language
docs.text:
1. Copy en_us.json to assets/questmod/lang/<code>.json (for example pt_br.json or fr_fr.json), inside the mod or a resource pack.
  2. Translate the values. Don't change the keys.
  3. Keep placeholders such as %s, %d and %1$s in place.

Percent signs

In texts with formatting, a literal % is written %% (for example "Total progress: %d%%").

docs.title: Changing a text without touching the mod
docs.text: Put a language file in a resource pack with only the keys you want to rewrite. It applies on top of the original.

docs.title: Translating datapack quests
docs.text:
In the name or description of a quest or section, a value starting with $ is a language key. This way the modpack can ship its quests translated:

{ "name": "$mypack.quest.zombies.name", "description": "$mypack.quest.zombies.desc", "objectives": [ ... ] }

And in assets/mypack/lang/en_us.json:

{ "mypack.quest.zombies.name": "Zombie hunter" }

If the key doesn't exist, the text is shown as is.

docs.title: Modpacks and datapacks
docs.text: QuestMod doesn't depend on an admin placing an NPC. A modpack can ship its quests ready-made and players can use them from the quest book.

docs.title: Quest book
docs.text:
• K key (rebindable) or the questmod:quest_book item (right-click). It opens the same panel without an NPC and shows quests with book or NPC and book access.
  • Welcome book: given on join according to giveBook in the server config (FIRST_JOIN, IF_MISSING or NEVER).
  • Turning it off: bookEnabled = false in the server config.
  • Making it craftable: the mod ships no recipe. Add one with a datapack, for example data/mypack/recipes/quest_book.json:
{
  "type": "minecraft:crafting_shapeless",
  "ingredients": [ { "item": "minecraft:book" }, { "item": "minecraft:feather" } ],
  "result": { "item": "questmod:quest_book" }
}

docs.title: Quests in JSON
docs.text:
Files data/<namespace>/questmod/quests/<name>.json. They load on their own when the world starts and with /reload, and are read-only in game. The quest ID is namespace:name and other quests can use it in requires.

{
  "name": "Zombie hunter",
  "description": "Kill zombies and eat something to recover.",
  "icon": "minecraft:iron_sword",
  "access": "both",
  "section": "mypack:combat",
  "objectives": [
    { "type": "kill", "target": "minecraft:zombie", "count": 20 },
    { "type": "eat", "target": "#minecraft:foods", "count": 5 }
  ],
  "milestones": [
    { "percent": 50, "rewards": [ { "item": "minecraft:bread", "count": 8 } ], "xp": 20 }
  ],
  "rewards": [
    { "item": "minecraft:diamond", "count": 3 },
    { "item": "minecraft:golden_apple", "count": 2 }
  ],
  "xp": 50,
  "show_reward": true
}

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Field Type Description name text Name. If it starts with $, the rest is a language key description text Description (also accepts $key) icon item ID List icon access npc · book · both Where it is offered from (default npc) section ID Section it belongs to scope individual · community Individual progress or a global counter min_contribution integer Community only: minimum contribution to claim auto_accept boolean Accepted automatically. In community quests it means "auto-join" auto_claim boolean Claimed automatically (doesn't apply to community quests) requires list of IDs Quests that must be claimed first (doesn't apply to community quests) objectives list (1 to 6) Each with type, target and count rewards list (up to 6) Each with item, count and optional nbt (SNBT) milestones list (up to 6) Each with percent (1 to 99), rewards and xp xp integer Experience of the final reward show_reward boolean If false, the player sees ???

Objective types: kill, break, eat, craft, smelt, deliver. The target is an ID or a #tag from any mod.

Autocomplete in VS Code

The wiki ships JSON schemas (quest and section). Associate them with data/*/questmod/quests/*.json and data/*/questmod/sections/*.json to get autocomplete and validation.

Invalid files don't break anything: they are skipped and the reason is written to the log.

docs.title: Sections in JSON
docs.text:
Files data/<namespace>/questmod/sections/<name>.json:

{ "name": "Create", "icon": "create:cogwheel", "order": 10 }

icon can be an item or an image (mypack:textures/gui/section/create.png). Quests use the section's ID in their section field.

docs.title: Create in game, ship as a datapack
docs.text:
Build the quests with the in-game editor and run:

/questmod export <namespace>

This generates questmod_export/<namespace>/ (with pack.mcmeta) with the quests and sections ready to drop into the modpack's datapacks. Afterwards, delete the quests from the world so you don't have them duplicated.

docs.title: Server configuration
docs.text:
In each world's serverconfig/questmod-server.toml. To set values in a modpack, put them in defaultconfigs/questmod-server.toml.

Option Default What it does adminPermissionLevel 2 Op level needed to manage singleplayerOwnerIsAdmin true In singleplayer, the owner is an admin even without cheats bookEnabled true Enables the quest book giveBook FIRST_JOIN When the book is given on join: NEVER, FIRST_JOIN, IF_MISSING

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: For admins. See Reference.

docs.title: NPCs
docs.text: The Quest Master is a motionless, invulnerable NPC that looks at players. Right-click opens its panel; shift + right-click (as an admin) opens its editor.

docs.title: Appearance
docs.text:
Mode What it does Default The mod's original skin Player skin Downloads a premium player's skin by name (the Me button uses yours) Skin from link A skin PNG (64x64 or 64x32) from an https link Resource pack texture A skin texture shipped in a resource pack or mod (modid:textures/...png) Mob / model from another mod The NPC is drawn with that mob's real model, from any installed mod. The NBT picks the variant Item / 3D model A floating item. With the NBT {CustomModelData:N} and a resource pack you can show any 3D model in JSON

You can also set a visible name, a scale (0.1 to 8, which also changes the hitbox) and slim arms for link or texture skins.

docs.title: NBT examples
docs.text:
• Librarian villager: {VillagerData:{profession:"minecraft:librarian",type:"minecraft:plains",level:1}}
  • Item with a custom model: {CustomModelData:1}

To pick the mob or item, use the little box next to the field: it opens the picker (inventory or the whole registry). From the inventory the NBT is copied too.

If something fails

If a mob's mod isn't on a client, or the model throws an error, that client sees the default skin instead of a crash. The mob's mod must be installed on the server and on the clients.

Privacy

Link skins are downloaded on the client and expose its IP to the link's owner. Each player can disable them with npc.allowUrlSkins in questmod-client.toml.

docs.title: Which quests it offers
docs.text:
In the Quests tab of the NPC editor:

  • All (default): offers every quest on the server, including ones you create later.
  • Only the chosen ones: tick single quests or whole sections. New quests you create from that NPC's panel are added automatically.

Quests live in a common pool: several NPCs can offer the same ones, and a player's progress is the same on all of them.

docs.title: Quest scroll
docs.text:
To copy one NPC's quest list to another (admins only):

Action Result Right-click an NPC with an empty scroll Copies its list Right-click another NPC with a loaded scroll Pastes the list (works for several NPCs) Shift + right-click an NPC Copies again (overwrites) Shift + right-click in the air Empties the scroll

What is pasted are references to the same quests, not copies: if you edit one, it changes on every NPC that offers it. The scroll copies sections too.

docs.title: "!" marker
docs.text: Above each NPC a red ! appears if there are new quests for you and a gold one if there are rewards to claim. It only counts that NPC's quests. It can be turned off with npc.showNpcMarker, and the textures (npc_marker_new.png and npc_marker_claim.png) can be replaced with a resource pack.

docs.title: Deleting an NPC
docs.text: In its editor, the red Delete NPC button asks for a second press to confirm. /kill works too.

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
A quest has 1 to 6 objectives and is completed when all are met.

Type Met when the player... kill kills an entity break breaks a block eat eats or drinks an item (food, potions, milk, mod drinks) craft crafts an item smelt takes an item out of a furnace deliver hands items to the NPC or book with the Deliver button (they are removed from the inventory)

docs.title: IDs and tags
docs.text:
The target is an ID (minecraft:zombie, create:andesite_alloy) or a tag with # (#minecraft:logs, #forge:ores). With a tag, a "break 20 logs" quest counts the logs from any mod that puts them in that tag.

You don't have to type anything in the editor: the picker on the right has three tabs, Inventory (your items), All (the whole registry, searchable, mods included) and Tags.

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• Up to 6 reward items, each with its amount and NBT (enchantments, potions, mod data). If the amount exceeds a stack, it is split up; whatever doesn't fit in the inventory drops on the ground.
  • Optional experience.
  • You can hide the reward (the player sees ??? until claiming).

docs.title: Milestones (percentage rewards)
docs.text:
A quest can give intermediate rewards when it reaches certain percentages. The final reward is 100%.

  • Up to 6 milestones, with a percentage from 1 to 99, and their own items and experience.
  • The percentage is the average progress of each objective, so all of them weigh the same. In a community quest it uses the global progress.
  • They are claimed with Claim milestone!, without waiting for the quest to be completed. Claiming the final reward also hands out any milestones left.
  • In the editor: Rewards page, the top button switches between the final reward and each milestone (+ creates one, ✕ deletes it).

docs.title: Requirements (chains)
docs.text: A quest can require that others are claimed. Until then it shows as Locked and you can see what is missing. Cycles are not allowed.

docs.title: Where it is offered from
docs.text:
Each quest chooses its access:

Access Meaning NPC only Accepted, delivered and claimed with an NPC that offers it Book only Only from the quest book (K key or item), no NPC NPC and book From either

docs.title: Automation
docs.text:
• Auto-accept: accepted as soon as it is unlocked, with no NPC or book. Great for tutorials or advancement-style progressions.
  • Auto-claim: when completed, the rewards go straight to the inventory.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
Sections group quests, for example one per mod. In the panel they appear as a strip of icons on the left, with a green dot if there are rewards to claim and a gold one if there are new quests.

  • Create (admins): the + button of the strip. Right-click a section to edit or delete it (its quests are left without a section).
  • Assign: in the quest editor, General page.
  • NPC by section: in the NPC's Quests tab you can tick whole sections. That NPC offers all their quests, including ones you create later.

docs.title: Community quests
docs.text:
A server-wide counter, and each player decides whether to take part.

  • Joining: the quest appears in Available with the global progress and a Join button. Only what you do after joining counts. Whoever doesn't join neither contributes nor spends items on deliveries.
  • Auto-join (optional): if you prefer an event where everyone is in by default, turn it on in the quest.
  • Claiming: when completed, only those who joined are notified in chat, and those who contributed at least the quest's minimum contribution can claim. Whoever didn't join, or didn't reach the minimum, sees it as closed. Nobody can join after it is completed.
  • Deliveries: delivery objectives work too: what each player hands in adds to the total and to their contribution.
  • Limitations: no requirements and no auto-claim.
  • Repeating an event: /questmod community reset <quest>.

Performance

Community progress is sent to players in batches, at most once per second, so hundreds of kills don't flood the network.

docs.title: Editing and deleting
docs.text: Admins see Edit and Delete (with confirmation) in the panel. Quests that come from a datapack are read-only in game.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: Key Action K Opens the quest book G Shows or hides each quest's steps in the HUD

docs.title: Client configuration
docs.text:
File config/questmod-client.toml.

Option Default Description hud.enabled true Shows the progress of active quests on screen hud.side LEFT HUD side: LEFT or RIGHT hud.maxQuests 5 Maximum quests shown in the HUD (1 to 10) hud.expanded false Shows each quest's steps separately (toggled with the G key) npc.allowUrlSkins true Allows downloading skins from https links set on NPCs by the server npc.showNpcMarker true Shows the ! above NPCs

docs.title: Server configuration
docs.text:
File serverconfig/questmod-server.toml of each world (or defaultconfigs/questmod-server.toml to set values in a modpack).

Option Default Description general.adminPermissionLevel 2 Op level needed to manage quests and NPCs (0 to 4) general.singleplayerOwnerIsAdmin true In a singleplayer world, the owner is an admin even without cheats general.bookEnabled true Enables the quest book (key and item) general.giveBook FIRST_JOIN When the book is given: NEVER, FIRST_JOIN (once per player) or IF_MISSING (on every join, if not carrying one)

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
For admins (the configured level, 2 by default; the console and command blocks use that same level).

Command What it does /questmod export <namespace> Exports the world's quests and sections as a datapack in questmod_export/<namespace>/ /questmod reset <players> [quest] Resets all progress, or a single quest /questmod complete <players> <quest> Marks a quest as completed /questmod community reset <quest> Resets a community quest for everyone (counter, contributions and claimed rewards)

Use the usual /reload to reload datapack quests.

docs.title: Items and entities
docs.text: ID What it is questmod:quest_npc The Quest Master (/summon questmod:quest_npc) questmod:quest_npc_spawn_egg Its spawn egg questmod:quest_scroll Quest scroll (copies and pastes lists between NPCs) questmod:quest_book Quest book (opens the panel without an NPC)

docs.title: Datapack paths
docs.text:
Path Content data/<ns>/questmod/quests/*.json Quests data/<ns>/questmod/sections/*.json Sections

The formats are in Modpacks and datapacks and there are JSON schemas to validate them.

docs.title: Theming
docs.text:
The whole look of the screens and the HUD comes from a normal resource, assets/questmod/theme.json. Any resource pack (including the server's) can override it, and you only need to put the keys you want to change: packs stack and anything missing uses the default theme. It reloads with F3 + T.

Example pack

In the repository, docs/ejemplo_tema/ is a complete resource pack (wood and gold) with textures ready to copy and modify.

docs.title: Colors and sizes
docs.text:
colors uses RRGGBB (opaque) or AARRGGBB. layout holds sizes in pixels (panel_width, list_width, hud_max_width...). The keys and their defaults are in the Reference.

{
  "colors": { "title": "55FFFF", "btn_accept": "AA00AA", "panel": "F00A0A2A" },
  "layout": { "panel_width": 420 }
}

docs.title: Textures (skins)
docs.text:
Each element can have an optional texture. If it has none, it is drawn with its usual color.

"skins": {
  "button": {
    "texture": "mypack:textures/gui/button.png",
    "width": 24, "height": 20,
    "border": 3,
    "hover":    { "v": 20 },
    "disabled": { "v": 40 }
  }
}
Field Description texture The image. The only required field (its size is detected automatically) u, v, width, height Which part of the image to use (default, all of it). Lets you put several states in one sheet border Border thickness for 9-slice: corners aren't distorted and the rest stretches, so one small PNG works at any size hover, disabled, selected State variants. They inherit the skin and only change what you specify (almost always v)

Setting "key": null removes the texture set by an earlier pack.

docs.title: Elements
docs.text:
Element Where it is used States panel Screen backgrounds normal picker Item picker background normal button All buttons normal, hover, disabled button_accept, button_claim, button_edit, button_delete, button_confirm, button_neutral Buttons by role (falls back to button) normal, hover entry Rows of the quest list and the picker normal, hover, selected section Cells of the section strip normal, hover, selected tab Available / In progress / Done tabs (with a texture the underline is hidden) normal, hover, selected slot Item boxes and picker cells normal, selected (active) checkbox List checkboxes normal, selected (checked) list_bg Background of lists with checkboxes normal bar_bg, bar_fill, bar_done Progress bars normal scroll Scrollbars normal hud_box, hud_step HUD boxes (quest and step) normal

Tips

  • Keep textures small and use border so they scale well.
  • A sheet with the three states stacked (normal, hover, disabled) is declared with "hover": {"v": 20}, "disabled": {"v": 40}.
  • The status color stripe of the rows is adjusted with layout.entry_stripe (0 hides it).
  • A broken skin (missing image, bad JSON) breaks nothing: it is reported in the log and the color is used.

docs.title: Section icons as images
docs.text: A section's icon can be an image instead of an item: type the PNG path (mypack:textures/gui/section/create.png) in the icon field. It is scaled to 16×16.

docs.title: Other textures
docs.text:
• NPC marker: textures/gui/npc_marker_new.png and npc_marker_claim.png.
  • Items and NPC: textures/item/quest_scroll.png, quest_book.png and textures/entity/quest_npc.png.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: The old panel_texture format (one stretched full image) still works.

docs.title: QuestMod
docs.text: QuestMod añade un sistema de misiones con estilo clásico a Minecraft Forge 1.20.1: un Maestro de misiones (NPC) que ofrece, entrega y premia misiones, con un panel claro en vez de un árbol gigante, y pensado para funcionar con cualquier mod.

docs.title: Qué incluye
docs.text:
• Misiones de varios tipos: matar, romper, consumir, craftear, fundir y entregar ítems. Los objetivos aceptan IDs de cualquier mod y tags (#minecraft:logs).
  • Varios objetivos por misión, varias recompensas con NBT, experiencia y hitos con premios por porcentaje.
  • Requisitos y cadenas de misiones, secciones (por ejemplo una por mod) y automatismos (aceptar y reclamar solas).
  • Misiones comunitarias con un contador global del servidor, donde cada jugador decide si participa.
  • NPC personalizables: skin de jugador, skin por enlace, textura de resource pack, modelo de otro mob de cualquier mod o un ítem con modelo 3D.
  • Libro de misiones (tecla o ítem) para usarlo sin NPC, y misiones por datapack para modpacks.
  • Editor dentro del juego con selector de ítems (inventario o todo el registro, incluidos los mods).
  • Personalizable: colores y texturas por resource pack, y traducible a cualquier idioma.

docs.title: Por dónde empezar
docs.text:
Si eres... Lee Jugador Primeros pasos Admin de un servidor Primeros pasos, Misiones y NPC Autor de un modpack Modpacks y datapacks Diseñador de resource packs Personalización Traductor Idiomas

Requisitos

Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47.2.0 o superior y Java 17. El mod debe estar instalado en el cliente y en el servidor.

docs.title: Con otros mods
docs.text:
• IDs de cualquier mod. Los objetivos aceptan mobs, bloques e ítems de cualquier mod instalado. El editor los lista (pestaña Todos del selector) y avisa en el chat si el objetivo no existe en el servidor.
  • Tags. Un tag como #forge:ores cuenta lo que cualquier mod meta en él, sin configurar nada.
  • Mobs y modelos de otros mods en los NPC. El NPC se dibuja con el renderer real del mob, así que funcionan también los mods con modelos propios (por ejemplo GeckoLib). Si falla, ese cliente ve la skin por defecto.
  • Ítems con modelos 3D. Con CustomModelData y un resource pack.

docs.title: Qué cuenta y qué no
docs.text:
Tipo Cuenta No cuenta kill Matar con armas, proyectiles y flechas del jugador Matar jugadores. Lo que hacen FakePlayer (turrets, deployers) break Romper bloques como jugador Lo que rompen máquinas de otros mods; romper bloques que un mod de protección impide eat Comida y también bebidas (pociones, leche, bebidas de mods) Lo que consume otro ser craft Craftear en mesa o menús de crafteo Máquinas que no usan el crafteo normal smelt Sacar el resultado de un horno Lo que mueven los hoppers u otras automatizaciones deliver Entregar con el botón del panel Soltar ítems al suelo

Las acciones de jugadores falsos (FakePlayer: deployers, turrets, quarries) no suman progreso. Los eventos de matar y romper se cuentan con prioridad baja: si un mod de protección (claims) cancela la acción, no cuenta.

docs.title: Cliente y servidor
docs.text: El mod debe estar en ambos lados y con la misma versión. Los mods de mobs, bloques o ítems que uses en una misión deben estar en ambos lados también (si no, el servidor o el cliente no reconocerán el ID).

docs.title: Mundos existentes
docs.text: Al actualizar, las misiones y el progreso anteriores se migran solos. Las misiones antiguas quedan con acceso Solo NPC, y los NPC existentes siguen ofreciendo todas las misiones.

docs.title: Preguntas frecuentes
docs.text:
No puedo editar nada en mi mundo en solitario

En un mundo en solitario el dueño es admin si singleplayerOwnerIsAdmin está en true (por defecto). Un modpack puede haberlo puesto en false en defaultconfigs/questmod-server.toml. Cámbialo en serverconfig/questmod-server.toml de tu mundo, o activa los cheats.

No veo el libro de misiones / la tecla K no hace nada

Comprueba bookEnabled y giveBook en la config del servidor. Además, el libro solo muestra misiones con acceso Solo libro o NPC y libro: una misión Solo NPC no aparece.

Mi misión no avanza
  • Si el objetivo no existe en el servidor (falta el mod o el ID/tag está mal escrito), al guardar recibiste un aviso en el chat y ese objetivo no avanza.
  • Debes haber aceptado la misión (en las comunitarias, unirte).
  • Las acciones de FakePlayer y lo que cancele un mod de protección no cuentan. Ver Compatibilidad.
El botón Aceptar o Reclamar no hace nada

Con un NPC debes estar a menos de 10 bloques y ese NPC debe ofrecer la misión (revisa su pestaña Misiones). Una misión Bloqueada pide completar antes sus requisitos.

Una misión comunitaria no suma

Solo cuenta lo que haces después de unirte. Pulsa Unirse en el panel.

Un NPC se ve con la skin por defecto

Puede ser que el mod del mob no esté en tu cliente, que el modelo haya fallado, o que las skins por enlace estén desactivadas (npc.allowUrlSkins). Una skin de jugador tarda un instante en descargarse.

Mi misión de datapack no aparece

Revisa el log: los archivos inválidos se omiten y se indica el motivo. Ejecuta /reload tras cambiar los archivos y comprueba la ruta data/<ns>/questmod/quests/. Las misiones de datapack son de solo lectura en el juego.

Mis texturas del tema no se aplican

Recarga con F3 + T, comprueba que el resource pack está activo y que theme.json está en assets/questmod/. Si una imagen no existe o el JSON está mal, el log lo indica y se usa el color de siempre.

¿Cómo reinicio el progreso de un jugador?

/questmod reset <jugador> para todo, o /questmod reset <jugador> <misión> para una sola. Para repetir una comunitaria para todos: /questmod community reset <misión>.

¿Qué pasa con mis misiones al actualizar?

Se migran solas. Las misiones antiguas quedan como Solo NPC, y los NPC existentes siguen ofreciendo todo. Actualiza cliente y servidor a la vez.

docs.title: Para jugadores
docs.text:
• Abrir las misiones: clic derecho a un Maestro de misiones, o la tecla K / el ítem Libro de misiones si el servidor lo permite.
  • El panel: la lista de misiones está a la izquierda y el detalle a la derecha. Las pestañas separan Disponibles, En curso y Hechas. Si hay secciones, aparecen como íconos a la izquierda.
  • Aceptar, entregar y reclamar: pulsa Aceptar en una misión disponible. Cuando cumplas sus objetivos aparece ¡Reclamar! y recibes los premios. Algunas misiones piden Entregar ítems al NPC. Para aceptar, entregar o reclamar con un NPC debes estar a menos de 10 bloques de él.
  • HUD: las misiones aceptadas se muestran en un lateral de la pantalla. Con G se despliega cada paso por separado.
  • Marcador: sobre un NPC, un ! rojo indica misiones nuevas y uno dorado, premios por reclamar.

Misiones comunitarias

Una misión comunitaria tiene un contador compartido por todo el servidor. Pulsa Unirse para participar: solo cuenta lo que hagas después de unirte.

docs.title: 1. Consigue un NPC
docs.text: Usa el huevo Maestro de misiones (pestaña de herramientas del creativo) o /summon questmod:quest_npc.

docs.title: 2. Configúralo
docs.text:
Shift + clic derecho al NPC (siendo admin) abre su editor, con dos pestañas:

  • Aspecto: nombre, skin, modelo de otro mob o ítem, escala. Ver NPC.
  • Misiones: qué misiones ofrece (todas, o solo las que elijas).

docs.title: 3. Crea una misión
docs.text:
Clic derecho al NPC y pulsa + Nueva misión. El editor tiene cuatro páginas:

  1. General: nombre, descripción, ícono, sección, desde dónde se ofrece y tipo.
  2. Objetivos: hasta 6. Pulsa el cuadrito, elige un mob, bloque o ítem en el panel de la derecha y pon la cantidad.
  3. Requisitos: misiones que deben estar reclamadas antes.
  4. Premios: ítems, experiencia y hitos.

Pulsa Guardar. Si un mob o ítem no existe en el servidor (por ejemplo, falta el mod), la misión se guarda igual pero recibes un aviso en el chat.

docs.title: ¿Quién es admin?
docs.text: Un operador con el nivel configurado (2 por defecto) y, en un mundo en solitario, también el dueño del mundo aunque no tenga cheats. Se puede cambiar en la configuración del servidor.

docs.title: Requisitos
docs.text:
• Minecraft 1.20.1 con Forge 47.2.0 o superior.
  • Java 17.
  • El mod debe estar instalado en el servidor y en todos los clientes. Si las versiones no coinciden, el cliente no podrá entrar (el mod comprueba una versión de protocolo de red).

docs.title: Pasos
docs.text:
1. Descarga el .jar desde CurseForge.
  2. Cópialo a la carpeta mods/ del cliente y del servidor.
  3. Inicia el juego. Se crean los archivos de configuración.

docs.title: Archivos de configuración
docs.text:
Archivo Dónde Para qué config/questmod-client.toml Cliente HUD, descarga de skins y marcador ! de los NPC serverconfig/questmod-server.toml Cada mundo Quién es admin, libro de misiones y libro de bienvenida defaultconfigs/questmod-server.toml Servidor o modpack Valores por defecto de la config del servidor para mundos nuevos

Las opciones están descritas en la Referencia.

docs.title: Teclas
docs.text:
Tecla Acción K Abre el libro de misiones (sin NPC) G Muestra u oculta los pasos de cada misión en el HUD

Se pueden cambiar en Opciones → Controles → QuestMod.

docs.title: Actualizar desde una versión anterior
docs.text: Las misiones y el progreso de versiones anteriores se leen sin problema: el progreso se migra solo la primera vez que un jugador entra. Como el protocolo de red cambia entre versiones, actualiza el mod a la vez en el servidor y en los clientes.

docs.title: Idiomas
docs.text: Todos los textos del mod (pantallas, mensajes del servidor, ítems, teclas) son claves de traducción en assets/questmod/lang/.

docs.title: Idiomas incluidos
docs.text: Inglés (en_us) y español (es_mx, es_es, es_ar, es_cl, es_uy, es_ve). Cada jugador ve el mod en su idioma, aunque el servidor esté en otro: los mensajes del servidor viajan como claves y los traduce cada cliente. Los idiomas sin traducción caen a inglés.

docs.title: Añadir un idioma
docs.text:
1. Copia en_us.json a assets/questmod/lang/<codigo>.json (por ejemplo pt_br.json o fr_fr.json), dentro del mod o de un resource pack.
  2. Traduce los valores. No cambies las claves.
  3. Mantén los marcadores como %s, %d y %1$s en su lugar.

Porcentajes

En los textos con formato, un % literal se escribe %% (por ejemplo "Progreso total: %d%%").

docs.title: Cambiar un texto sin tocar el mod
docs.text: Pon un archivo de idioma en un resource pack con solo las claves que quieras reescribir. Se aplica por encima del original.

docs.title: Traducir misiones de un datapack
docs.text:
En el name o la description de una misión o sección, un valor que empiece con $ es una clave de idioma. Así el modpack puede traer sus misiones traducidas:

{ "name": "$mipack.quest.zombis.name", "description": "$mipack.quest.zombis.desc", "objectives": [ ... ] }

Y en assets/mipack/lang/es_es.json:

{ "mipack.quest.zombis.name": "Cazador de zombis" }

Si la clave no existe, se muestra el texto tal cual.

docs.title: Modpacks y datapacks
docs.text: QuestMod no depende de que un admin ponga un NPC. Un modpack puede traer sus misiones ya hechas y los jugadores usarlas desde el libro de misiones.

docs.title: Libro de misiones
docs.text:
• Tecla K (cambiable) o el ítem questmod:quest_book (clic derecho). Abre el mismo panel sin NPC y muestra las misiones con acceso libro o NPC y libro.
  • Libro de bienvenida: se entrega al entrar según giveBook en la config del servidor (FIRST_JOIN, IF_MISSING o NEVER).
  • Apagarlo: bookEnabled = false en la config del servidor.
  • Hacerlo crafteable: el mod no trae receta. Añade una con un datapack, por ejemplo data/mipack/recipes/quest_book.json:
{
  "type": "minecraft:crafting_shapeless",
  "ingredients": [ { "item": "minecraft:book" }, { "item": "minecraft:feather" } ],
  "result": { "item": "questmod:quest_book" }
}

docs.title: Misiones en JSON
docs.text:
Archivos data/<namespace>/questmod/quests/<nombre>.json. Se cargan solos al iniciar el mundo y con /reload, y en el juego son de solo lectura. El ID de la misión es namespace:nombre y otras misiones pueden usarlo en requires.

{
  "name": "Cazador de zombis",
  "description": "Elimina zombis y come algo para recuperar fuerzas.",
  "icon": "minecraft:iron_sword",
  "access": "both",
  "section": "mipack:combate",
  "objectives": [
    { "type": "kill", "target": "minecraft:zombie", "count": 20 },
    { "type": "eat", "target": "#minecraft:foods", "count": 5 }
  ],
  "milestones": [
    { "percent": 50, "rewards": [ { "item": "minecraft:bread", "count": 8 } ], "xp": 20 }
  ],
  "rewards": [
    { "item": "minecraft:diamond", "count": 3 },
    { "item": "minecraft:golden_apple", "count": 2 }
  ],
  "xp": 50,
  "show_reward": true
}

docs.title: Campos
docs.text:
Campo Tipo Descripción name texto Nombre. Si empieza con $, el resto es una clave de idioma description texto Descripción (también acepta $clave) icon ID de ítem Ícono de la lista access npc · book · both Desde dónde se ofrece (por defecto npc) section ID Sección a la que pertenece scope individual · community Progreso individual o contador global min_contribution entero Solo comunitarias: aporte mínimo para reclamar auto_accept booleano Se acepta sola. En comunitarias significa "unirse sola" auto_claim booleano Se reclama sola (no aplica a comunitarias) requires lista de IDs Misiones que deben estar reclamadas (no aplica a comunitarias) objectives lista (1 a 6) Cada uno con type, target y count rewards lista (hasta 6) Cada uno con item, count y nbt opcional (SNBT) milestones lista (hasta 6) Cada uno con percent (1 a 99), rewards y xp xp entero Experiencia del premio final show_reward booleano Si es false, el jugador ve ???

Tipos de objetivo: kill, break, eat, craft, smelt, deliver. El target es un ID o un #tag de cualquier mod.

Autocompletado en VS Code

En la wiki hay esquemas JSON (misión y sección). Asócialos a data/*/questmod/quests/*.json y data/*/questmod/sections/*.json para tener autocompletado y validación.

Los archivos inválidos no rompen nada: se omiten y el motivo queda en el log.

docs.title: Secciones en JSON
docs.text:
Archivos data/<namespace>/questmod/sections/<nombre>.json:

{ "name": "Create", "icon": "create:cogwheel", "order": 10 }

icon puede ser un ítem o una imagen (mipack:textures/gui/seccion/create.png). Las misiones usan el ID de la sección en su campo section.

docs.title: Crear en el juego y repartir como datapack
docs.text:
Arma las misiones con el editor del juego y ejecuta:

/questmod export <namespace>

Se genera questmod_export/<namespace>/ (con pack.mcmeta) con las misiones y secciones listas para meter en los datapacks del modpack. Después borra las misiones del mundo para no tenerlas duplicadas.

docs.title: Configuración del servidor
docs.text:
En serverconfig/questmod-server.toml de cada mundo. Para fijar valores en un modpack, ponlos en defaultconfigs/questmod-server.toml.

Opción Por defecto Qué hace adminPermissionLevel 2 Nivel de op necesario para administrar singleplayerOwnerIsAdmin true En solitario, el dueño es admin aunque no tenga cheats bookEnabled true Activa el libro de misiones giveBook FIRST_JOIN Cuándo se entrega el libro al entrar: NEVER, FIRST_JOIN, IF_MISSING

docs.title: Comandos
docs.text: Para admins. Ver Referencia.

docs.title: NPC
docs.text: El Maestro de misiones es un NPC inmóvil e invulnerable que mira a los jugadores. Clic derecho abre su panel; shift + clic derecho (siendo admin) abre su editor.

docs.title: Aspecto
docs.text:
Modo Qué hace Por defecto La skin original del mod Skin de jugador Descarga la skin de un jugador premium por nombre (el botón Yo pone la tuya) Skin por enlace Un PNG de skin (64x64 o 64x32) desde un enlace https Textura de resource pack Una textura de skin que venga en un resource pack o mod (modid:textures/...png) Mob / modelo de otro mod El NPC se dibuja con el modelo real de ese mob, de cualquier mod instalado. El NBT elige la variante Ítem / modelo 3D Un ítem flotante. Con el NBT {CustomModelData:N} y un resource pack se puede mostrar cualquier modelo 3D en JSON

Además puedes poner nombre visible, escala (de 0.1 a 8, también cambia la hitbox) y brazos finos para skins por enlace o textura.

docs.title: Ejemplos de NBT
docs.text:
• Aldeano bibliotecario: {VillagerData:{profession:"minecraft:librarian",type:"minecraft:plains",level:1}}
  • Ítem con modelo personalizado: {CustomModelData:1}

Para elegir el mob o el ítem usa el cuadrito junto al campo: abre el selector (inventario o todo el registro). Desde el inventario se copia también el NBT.

Si algo falla

Si el mod de un mob no está en un cliente, o el modelo da un error, ese cliente ve la skin por defecto en vez de un fallo. El mod del mob debe estar instalado en el servidor y en los clientes.

Privacidad

Las skins por enlace se descargan en el cliente y exponen su IP al dueño del enlace. Cada jugador puede desactivarlas con npc.allowUrlSkins en questmod-client.toml.

docs.title: Qué misiones ofrece
docs.text:
En la pestaña Misiones del editor del NPC:

  • Todas (por defecto): ofrece cada misión del servidor, incluidas las que crees después.
  • Solo las elegidas: marca misiones sueltas o secciones enteras. Las misiones nuevas que crees desde el panel de ese NPC se añaden solas.

Las misiones viven en un fondo común: varios NPC pueden ofrecer las mismas, y el progreso del jugador es el mismo en todos.

docs.title: Pergamino de misiones
docs.text:
Para copiar la lista de misiones de un NPC a otro (solo admins):

Acción Resultado Clic derecho a un NPC con el pergamino vacío Copia su lista Clic derecho a otro NPC con el pergamino cargado Pega la lista (sirve para varios NPC) Shift + clic derecho a un NPC Copia de nuevo (sobrescribe) Shift + clic derecho al aire Vacía el pergamino

Se pegan referencias a las mismas misiones, no copias: si editas una, cambia en todos los NPC que la ofrecen. El pergamino copia también las secciones.

docs.title: Marcador "!"
docs.text: Sobre cada NPC aparece un ! rojo si hay misiones nuevas para ti y uno dorado si hay premios por reclamar. Solo cuenta las misiones de ese NPC. Se apaga con npc.showNpcMarker, y las texturas (npc_marker_new.png y npc_marker_claim.png) se pueden reemplazar con un resource pack.

docs.title: Eliminar un NPC
docs.text: En su editor, el botón rojo Eliminar NPC pide una segunda pulsación para confirmar. También funciona /kill.

docs.title: Objetivos
docs.text:
Una misión tiene de 1 a 6 objetivos y se completa cuando se cumplen todos.

Tipo Se cumple cuando el jugador... kill (Mata) mata una entidad break (Rompe) rompe un bloque eat (Consume) come o bebe un ítem (comida, pociones, leche, bebidas de mods) craft (Craftea) craftea un ítem smelt (Funde) saca un ítem de un horno deliver (Entrega) entrega ítems al NPC o al libro con el botón Entregar (se quitan del inventario)

docs.title: IDs y tags
docs.text:
El objetivo es un ID (minecraft:zombie, create:andesite_alloy) o un tag con # (#minecraft:logs, #forge:ores). Con un tag, una misión de "romper 20 troncos" cuenta los troncos de cualquier mod que los meta en ese tag.

En el editor no hace falta escribir nada: el selector a la derecha tiene tres pestañas, Inventario (tus ítems), Todos (todo el registro, con buscador, mods incluidos) y Tags.

docs.title: Premios
docs.text:
• Hasta 6 ítems de recompensa, cada uno con su cantidad y su NBT (encantamientos, pociones, datos de mods). Si la cantidad pasa de un stack, se reparte; lo que no quepa en el inventario cae al suelo.
  • Experiencia opcional.
  • Puedes ocultar el premio (el jugador ve ??? hasta reclamar).

docs.title: Hitos (premios por porcentaje)
docs.text:
Una misión puede dar premios intermedios al llegar a ciertos porcentajes. El premio final es el 100%.

  • Hasta 6 hitos, con porcentaje de 1 a 99, ítems y experiencia propios.
  • El porcentaje es el promedio del avance de cada objetivo, así todos pesan igual. En una comunitaria cuenta el avance global.
  • Se reclaman con ¡Reclamar hito!, sin esperar a completar la misión. Al reclamar el premio final se entregan los hitos que faltaran.
  • En el editor: página Premios, el botón de arriba cambia entre el premio final y cada hito (+ crea uno, ✕ lo borra).

docs.title: Requisitos (cadenas)
docs.text: Una misión puede exigir que otras estén reclamadas. Mientras tanto aparece como Bloqueada y se ve qué falta. No se permiten ciclos.

docs.title: Desde dónde se ofrece
docs.text:
Cada misión elige su acceso:

Acceso Significado Solo NPC Se acepta, entrega y reclama con un NPC que la ofrezca Solo libro Solo desde el libro de misiones (tecla K o ítem), sin NPC NPC y libro Desde cualquiera de los dos

docs.title: Automatismos
docs.text:
• Aceptar sola: se acepta en cuanto está desbloqueada, sin NPC ni libro. Ideal para tutoriales o progresiones tipo logros.
  • Reclamar sola: al completarse, los premios van directo al inventario.

docs.title: Secciones
docs.text:
Las secciones agrupan misiones, por ejemplo una por mod. En el panel aparecen como una tira de íconos a la izquierda, con un punto verde si hay premios por reclamar y uno dorado si hay misiones nuevas.

  • Crear (admins): el botón + de la tira. Clic derecho sobre una sección para editarla o borrarla (sus misiones quedan sin sección).
  • Asignar: en el editor de misión, página General.
  • NPC por sección: en la pestaña Misiones del NPC puedes marcar secciones enteras. Ese NPC ofrece todas sus misiones, también las que crees después.

docs.title: Misiones comunitarias
docs.text:
Un contador global del servidor, y cada jugador decide si participa.

  • Unirse: la misión aparece en Disponibles con el avance global y el botón Unirse. Solo cuenta lo que hagas después de unirte. Quien no se une no aporta ni gasta ítems en entregas.
  • Unirse sola (opcional): si prefieres un evento donde todos entren por defecto, actívalo en la misión.
  • Reclamar: al completarse se avisa por chat solo a quienes se unieron, y reclaman los que aportaron al menos el aporte mínimo de la misión. Quien no se unió, o no llegó al mínimo, la ve como cerrada. Nadie puede unirse después de completada.
  • Entregas: los objetivos de entrega también valen: lo que entrega cada jugador suma al total y a su aporte.
  • Limitaciones: no tienen requisitos ni reclamo automático.
  • Repetir un evento: /questmod community reset <misión>.

Rendimiento

El avance de las comunitarias se envía a los jugadores en bloque, como máximo una vez por segundo, así cientos de kills no saturan la red.

docs.title: Editar y borrar
docs.text: Los admins ven Editar y Borrar (con confirmación) en el panel. Las misiones que vienen de un datapack son de solo lectura en el juego.

docs.title: Controles
docs.text: Tecla Acción K Abre el libro de misiones G Muestra u oculta los pasos de cada misión en el HUD

docs.title: Configuración del cliente
docs.text:
Archivo config/questmod-client.toml.

Opción Por defecto Descripción hud.enabled true Muestra el progreso de las misiones activas en pantalla hud.side LEFT Lado del HUD: LEFT o RIGHT hud.maxQuests 5 Máximo de misiones visibles en el HUD (1 a 10) hud.expanded false Muestra los pasos de cada misión por separado (lo alterna la tecla G) npc.allowUrlSkins true Permite descargar skins desde enlaces https que el servidor ponga en los NPC npc.showNpcMarker true Muestra el ! sobre los NPC

docs.title: Configuración del servidor
docs.text:
Archivo serverconfig/questmod-server.toml de cada mundo (o defaultconfigs/questmod-server.toml para fijar valores en un modpack).

Opción Por defecto Descripción general.adminPermissionLevel 2 Nivel de op necesario para administrar misiones y NPC (0 a 4) general.singleplayerOwnerIsAdmin true En un mundo en solitario, el dueño es admin aunque no tenga cheats general.bookEnabled true Activa el libro de misiones (tecla e ítem) general.giveBook FIRST_JOIN Cuándo se entrega el libro: NEVER, FIRST_JOIN (una vez por jugador) o IF_MISSING (en cada entrada, si no lo lleva)

docs.title: Comandos
docs.text:
Para admins (nivel configurado, 2 por defecto; la consola y los command blocks usan ese mismo nivel).

Comando Qué hace /questmod export <namespace> Exporta las misiones y secciones del mundo como datapack en questmod_export/<namespace>/ /questmod reset <jugadores> [misión] Reinicia el progreso de todo, o de una misión /questmod complete <jugadores> <misión> Marca una misión como completada /questmod community reset <misión> Reinicia una misión comunitaria para todos (contador, aportes y premios reclamados)

Para recargar las misiones de datapack se usa el /reload de siempre.

docs.title: Personalización
docs.text:
Todo el aspecto de las pantallas y del HUD sale de un recurso normal, assets/questmod/theme.json. Cualquier resource pack (incluido el del servidor) puede sobrescribirlo, y basta con poner solo las claves que quieras cambiar: los packs se apilan y lo que falte usa el tema por defecto. Se recarga con F3 + T.

Pack de ejemplo

En el repositorio, docs/ejemplo_tema/ es un resource pack completo (madera y dorado) con texturas listas para copiar y modificar.

docs.title: Colores y medidas
docs.text:
colors usa RRGGBB (opaco) o AARRGGBB. layout son medidas en píxeles (panel_width, list_width, hud_max_width...). Las claves y sus valores por defecto están en la Referencia.

{
  "colors": { "title": "55FFFF", "btn_accept": "AA00AA", "panel": "F00A0A2A" },
  "layout": { "panel_width": 420 }
}

docs.title: Texturas (skins)
docs.text:
Cada elemento puede tener una textura opcional. Si no la tiene, se dibuja con su color de siempre.

"skins": {
  "button": {
    "texture": "mipack:textures/gui/boton.png",
    "width": 24, "height": 20,
    "border": 3,
    "hover":    { "v": 20 },
    "disabled": { "v": 40 }
  }
}
Campo Descripción texture La imagen. Es lo único obligatorio (el tamaño se detecta solo) u, v, width, height Qué parte de la imagen usar (por defecto, toda). Permite varios estados en una hoja border Grosor del borde para 9-slice: las esquinas no se deforman y el resto se estira, así un PNG pequeño sirve para cualquier tamaño hover, disabled, selected Variantes por estado. Heredan lo del skin y solo cambian lo que indiques (casi siempre v)

Poner "clave": null quita la textura que haya puesto un pack anterior.

Consejos

  • Haz las texturas pequeñas y usa border para que escalen bien.
  • Una hoja con los tres estados apilados (normal, hover, disabled) se indica con "hover": {"v": 20}, "disabled": {"v": 40}.
  • La franja de color de estado de las filas se ajusta con layout.entry_stripe (0 la oculta).
  • Los errores de un skin (imagen que no existe, JSON mal) no rompen nada: se avisa en el log y se usa el color.

docs.title: Íconos de sección como imagen
docs.text: El ícono de una sección puede ser una imagen en vez de un ítem: escribe la ruta del PNG (mipack:textures/gui/seccion/create.png) en el campo del ícono. Se escala a 16×16.

docs.title: Otras texturas
docs.text:
• Marcador de los NPC: textures/gui/npc_marker_new.png y npc_marker_claim.png.
  • Ítems y NPC: textures/item/quest_scroll.png, quest_book.png y textures/entity/quest_npc.png.

docs.title: Compatibilidad
docs.text: El formato antiguo panel_texture (una imagen completa estirada) sigue funcionando.

docs.title: QuestMod
docs.text: QuestMod adds a classic-style quest system to Minecraft Forge 1.20.1: a Quest Master (NPC) that offers, takes in and rewards quests, with a clear panel instead of a giant tree, built to work with any mod.

docs.title: What it includes
docs.text:
• Several quest types: kill, break, consume, craft, smelt and deliver items. Objectives accept IDs from any mod and tags (#minecraft:logs).
  • Several objectives per quest, several rewards with NBT, experience and milestones with percentage rewards.
  • Requirements and chains of quests, sections (for example one per mod) and automation (auto-accept and auto-claim).
  • Community quests with a server-wide counter, where each player decides whether to take part.
  • Customizable NPCs: player skin, skin from a link, resource pack texture, the model of another mob from any mod, or an item with a 3D model.
  • Quest book (key or item) to use it without NPCs, and datapack quests for modpacks.
  • In-game editor with an item picker (inventory or the whole registry, mods included).
  • Customizable: colors and textures through resource packs, and translatable to any language.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
If you are... Read A player Getting started A server admin Getting started, Quests and NPCs A modpack author Modpacks and datapacks A resource pack designer Theming A translator Languages

Requirements

Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47.2.0 or newer, and Java 17. The mod must be installed on both the client and the server.

docs.title: With other mods
docs.text:
• IDs from any mod. Objectives accept mobs, blocks and items from any installed mod. The editor lists them (the picker's All tab) and warns in chat if the target doesn't exist on the server.
  • Tags. A tag like #forge:ores counts whatever any mod puts in it, with no setup.
  • Mobs and models from other mods on NPCs. The NPC is drawn with the mob's real renderer, so mods with their own models (for example GeckoLib) work too. If it fails, that client sees the default skin.
  • Items with 3D models. With CustomModelData and a resource pack.

docs.title: What counts and what doesn't
docs.text:
Type Counts Doesn't count kill Kills with weapons and projectiles/arrows fired by the player Killing players. What a FakePlayer does (turrets, deployers) break Breaking blocks as a player What machines from other mods break; breaking blocks a protection mod prevents eat Food and also drinks (potions, milk, mod drinks) What another creature consumes craft Crafting at a table or crafting menus Machines that don't use normal crafting smelt Taking the result out of a furnace What hoppers or other automation move deliver Delivering with the panel button Dropping items on the ground

Actions by fake players (FakePlayer: deployers, turrets, quarries) don't add progress. Kill and break events are counted with low priority: if a protection (claims) mod cancels the action, it doesn't count.

docs.title: Client and server
docs.text: The mod must be on both sides with the same version. Mods for the mobs, blocks or items you use in a quest must also be on both sides (otherwise the server or client won't recognize the ID).

docs.title: Existing worlds
docs.text: When updating, earlier quests and progress are migrated automatically. Old quests keep NPC only access, and existing NPCs keep offering all quests.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
I can't edit anything in my singleplayer world

In a singleplayer world the owner is an admin if singleplayerOwnerIsAdmin is true (the default). A modpack may have set it to false in defaultconfigs/questmod-server.toml. Change it in your world's serverconfig/questmod-server.toml, or enable cheats.

I can't see the quest book / the K key does nothing

Check bookEnabled and giveBook in the server config. Also, the book only shows quests with Book only or NPC and book access: an NPC only quest doesn't appear.

My quest doesn't advance
  • If the target doesn't exist on the server (a mod is missing or the ID/tag is misspelled), you got a warning in chat when saving and that objective won't advance.
  • You must have accepted the quest (in community quests, joined).
  • Actions by FakePlayers and anything a protection mod cancels don't count. See Compatibility.
The Accept or Claim button does nothing

With an NPC you must be within 10 blocks and that NPC must offer the quest (check its Quests tab). A Locked quest asks you to complete its requirements first.

A community quest doesn't add up

Only what you do after joining counts. Press Join in the panel.

An NPC shows the default skin

The mob's mod may not be on your client, the model may have failed, or link skins may be disabled (npc.allowUrlSkins). A player skin takes a moment to download.

My datapack quest doesn't show up

Check the log: invalid files are skipped and the reason is given. Run /reload after changing files and check the path data/<ns>/questmod/quests/. Datapack quests are read-only in game.

My theme textures aren't applied

Reload with F3 + T, check that the resource pack is active and that theme.json is in assets/questmod/. If an image is missing or the JSON is wrong, the log says so and the usual color is used.

How do I reset a player's progress?

/questmod reset <player> for everything, or /questmod reset <player> <quest> for one. To repeat a community quest for everyone: /questmod community reset <quest>.

What happens to my quests when updating?

They are migrated automatically. Old quests stay as NPC only, and existing NPCs keep offering everything. Update client and server at the same time.

docs.title: For players
docs.text:
• Opening quests: right-click a Quest Master, or use the K key / the Quest Book item if the server allows it.
  • The panel: the quest list is on the left and the details on the right. Tabs separate Available, In progress and Done. If there are sections, they appear as icons on the left.
  • Accept, deliver and claim: press Accept on an available quest. When you meet its objectives, Claim! appears and you get the rewards. Some quests ask you to Deliver items to the NPC. To accept, deliver or claim with an NPC you must be within 10 blocks of it.
  • HUD: accepted quests are shown on a side of the screen. Press G to expand each step separately.
  • Marker: above an NPC, a red ! means new quests and a gold one means rewards to claim.

Community quests

A community quest has a counter shared by the whole server. Press Join to take part: only what you do after joining counts.

docs.title: 1. Get an NPC
docs.text: Use the Quest Master egg (creative Tools tab) or /summon questmod:quest_npc.

docs.title: 2. Configure it
docs.text:
Shift + right-click the NPC (as an admin) opens its editor, with two tabs:

  • Appearance: name, skin, model of another mob or item, scale. See NPCs.
  • Quests: which quests it offers (all of them, or only the ones you pick).

docs.title: 3. Create a quest
docs.text:
Right-click the NPC and press + New quest. The editor has four pages:

  1. General: name, description, icon, section, where it is offered from, and type.
  2. Objectives: up to 6. Press the little box, pick a mob, block or item in the panel on the right, and set the amount.
  3. Requirements: quests that must be claimed first.
  4. Rewards: items, experience and milestones.

Press Save. If a mob or item doesn't exist on the server (for example a mod is missing), the quest is still saved but you get a warning in chat.

docs.title: Who is an admin?
docs.text: An operator with the configured level (2 by default) and, in a singleplayer world, also the world owner even without cheats. It can be changed in the server configuration.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Minecraft 1.20.1 with Forge 47.2.0 or newer.
  • Java 17.
  • The mod must be installed on the server and on every client. If the versions don't match, the client can't join (the mod checks a network protocol version).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Download the .jar from CurseForge.
  2. Copy it into the mods/ folder of the client and the server.
  3. Start the game. The configuration files are created.

docs.title: Configuration files
docs.text:
File Where What for config/questmod-client.toml Client HUD, skin downloads and the NPC ! marker serverconfig/questmod-server.toml Each world Who is an admin, the quest book and the welcome book defaultconfigs/questmod-server.toml Server or modpack Default server config values for new worlds

The options are described in the Reference.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
Key Action K Opens the quest book (no NPC needed) G Shows or hides each quest's steps in the HUD

They can be changed in Options → Controls → QuestMod.

docs.title: Updating from an earlier version
docs.text: Quests and progress from earlier versions are read without problems: progress is migrated automatically the first time a player joins. Because the network protocol changes between versions, update the mod on the server and on the clients at the same time.

docs.title: Languages
docs.text: All of the mod's texts (screens, server messages, items, keys) are translation keys in assets/questmod/lang/.

docs.title: Included languages
docs.text: English (en_us) and Spanish (es_mx, es_es, es_ar, es_cl, es_uy, es_ve). Each player sees the mod in their language even if the server is in another: server messages travel as keys and each client translates them. Languages without a translation fall back to English.

docs.title: Adding a language
docs.text:
1. Copy en_us.json to assets/questmod/lang/<code>.json (for example pt_br.json or fr_fr.json), inside the mod or a resource pack.
  2. Translate the values. Don't change the keys.
  3. Keep placeholders such as %s, %d and %1$s in place.

Percent signs

In texts with formatting, a literal % is written %% (for example "Total progress: %d%%").

docs.title: Changing a text without touching the mod
docs.text: Put a language file in a resource pack with only the keys you want to rewrite. It applies on top of the original.

docs.title: Translating datapack quests
docs.text:
In the name or description of a quest or section, a value starting with $ is a language key. This way the modpack can ship its quests translated:

{ "name": "$mypack.quest.zombies.name", "description": "$mypack.quest.zombies.desc", "objectives": [ ... ] }

And in assets/mypack/lang/en_us.json:

{ "mypack.quest.zombies.name": "Zombie hunter" }

If the key doesn't exist, the text is shown as is.

docs.title: Modpacks and datapacks
docs.text: QuestMod doesn't depend on an admin placing an NPC. A modpack can ship its quests ready-made and players can use them from the quest book.

docs.title: Quest book
docs.text:
• K key (rebindable) or the questmod:quest_book item (right-click). It opens the same panel without an NPC and shows quests with book or NPC and book access.
  • Welcome book: given on join according to giveBook in the server config (FIRST_JOIN, IF_MISSING or NEVER).
  • Turning it off: bookEnabled = false in the server config.
  • Making it craftable: the mod ships no recipe. Add one with a datapack, for example data/mypack/recipes/quest_book.json:
{
  "type": "minecraft:crafting_shapeless",
  "ingredients": [ { "item": "minecraft:book" }, { "item": "minecraft:feather" } ],
  "result": { "item": "questmod:quest_book" }
}

docs.title: Quests in JSON
docs.text:
Files data/<namespace>/questmod/quests/<name>.json. They load on their own when the world starts and with /reload, and are read-only in game. The quest ID is namespace:name and other quests can use it in requires.

{
  "name": "Zombie hunter",
  "description": "Kill zombies and eat something to recover.",
  "icon": "minecraft:iron_sword",
  "access": "both",
  "section": "mypack:combat",
  "objectives": [
    { "type": "kill", "target": "minecraft:zombie", "count": 20 },
    { "type": "eat", "target": "#minecraft:foods", "count": 5 }
  ],
  "milestones": [
    { "percent": 50, "rewards": [ { "item": "minecraft:bread", "count": 8 } ], "xp": 20 }
  ],
  "rewards": [
    { "item": "minecraft:diamond", "count": 3 },
    { "item": "minecraft:golden_apple", "count": 2 }
  ],
  "xp": 50,
  "show_reward": true
}

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Field Type Description name text Name. If it starts with $, the rest is a language key description text Description (also accepts $key) icon item ID List icon access npc · book · both Where it is offered from (default npc) section ID Section it belongs to scope individual · community Individual progress or a global counter min_contribution integer Community only: minimum contribution to claim auto_accept boolean Accepted automatically. In community quests it means "auto-join" auto_claim boolean Claimed automatically (doesn't apply to community quests) requires list of IDs Quests that must be claimed first (doesn't apply to community quests) objectives list (1 to 6) Each with type, target and count rewards list (up to 6) Each with item, count and optional nbt (SNBT) milestones list (up to 6) Each with percent (1 to 99), rewards and xp xp integer Experience of the final reward show_reward boolean If false, the player sees ???

Objective types: kill, break, eat, craft, smelt, deliver. The target is an ID or a #tag from any mod.

Autocomplete in VS Code

The wiki ships JSON schemas (quest and section). Associate them with data/*/questmod/quests/*.json and data/*/questmod/sections/*.json to get autocomplete and validation.

Invalid files don't break anything: they are skipped and the reason is written to the log.

docs.title: Sections in JSON
docs.text:
Files data/<namespace>/questmod/sections/<name>.json:

{ "name": "Create", "icon": "create:cogwheel", "order": 10 }

icon can be an item or an image (mypack:textures/gui/section/create.png). Quests use the section's ID in their section field.

docs.title: Create in game, ship as a datapack
docs.text:
Build the quests with the in-game editor and run:

/questmod export <namespace>

This generates questmod_export/<namespace>/ (with pack.mcmeta) with the quests and sections ready to drop into the modpack's datapacks. Afterwards, delete the quests from the world so you don't have them duplicated.

docs.title: Server configuration
docs.text:
In each world's serverconfig/questmod-server.toml. To set values in a modpack, put them in defaultconfigs/questmod-server.toml.

Option Default What it does adminPermissionLevel 2 Op level needed to manage singleplayerOwnerIsAdmin true In singleplayer, the owner is an admin even without cheats bookEnabled true Enables the quest book giveBook FIRST_JOIN When the book is given on join: NEVER, FIRST_JOIN, IF_MISSING

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: For admins. See Reference.

docs.title: NPCs
docs.text: The Quest Master is a motionless, invulnerable NPC that looks at players. Right-click opens its panel; shift + right-click (as an admin) opens its editor.

docs.title: Appearance
docs.text:
Mode What it does Default The mod's original skin Player skin Downloads a premium player's skin by name (the Me button uses yours) Skin from link A skin PNG (64x64 or 64x32) from an https link Resource pack texture A skin texture shipped in a resource pack or mod (modid:textures/...png) Mob / model from another mod The NPC is drawn with that mob's real model, from any installed mod. The NBT picks the variant Item / 3D model A floating item. With the NBT {CustomModelData:N} and a resource pack you can show any 3D model in JSON

You can also set a visible name, a scale (0.1 to 8, which also changes the hitbox) and slim arms for link or texture skins.

docs.title: NBT examples
docs.text:
• Librarian villager: {VillagerData:{profession:"minecraft:librarian",type:"minecraft:plains",level:1}}
  • Item with a custom model: {CustomModelData:1}

To pick the mob or item, use the little box next to the field: it opens the picker (inventory or the whole registry). From the inventory the NBT is copied too.

If something fails

If a mob's mod isn't on a client, or the model throws an error, that client sees the default skin instead of a crash. The mob's mod must be installed on the server and on the clients.

Privacy

Link skins are downloaded on the client and expose its IP to the link's owner. Each player can disable them with npc.allowUrlSkins in questmod-client.toml.

docs.title: Which quests it offers
docs.text:
In the Quests tab of the NPC editor:

  • All (default): offers every quest on the server, including ones you create later.
  • Only the chosen ones: tick single quests or whole sections. New quests you create from that NPC's panel are added automatically.

Quests live in a common pool: several NPCs can offer the same ones, and a player's progress is the same on all of them.

docs.title: Quest scroll
docs.text:
To copy one NPC's quest list to another (admins only):

Action Result Right-click an NPC with an empty scroll Copies its list Right-click another NPC with a loaded scroll Pastes the list (works for several NPCs) Shift + right-click an NPC Copies again (overwrites) Shift + right-click in the air Empties the scroll

What is pasted are references to the same quests, not copies: if you edit one, it changes on every NPC that offers it. The scroll copies sections too.

docs.title: "!" marker
docs.text: Above each NPC a red ! appears if there are new quests for you and a gold one if there are rewards to claim. It only counts that NPC's quests. It can be turned off with npc.showNpcMarker, and the textures (npc_marker_new.png and npc_marker_claim.png) can be replaced with a resource pack.

docs.title: Deleting an NPC
docs.text: In its editor, the red Delete NPC button asks for a second press to confirm. /kill works too.

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
A quest has 1 to 6 objectives and is completed when all are met.

Type Met when the player... kill kills an entity break breaks a block eat eats or drinks an item (food, potions, milk, mod drinks) craft crafts an item smelt takes an item out of a furnace deliver hands items to the NPC or book with the Deliver button (they are removed from the inventory)

docs.title: IDs and tags
docs.text:
The target is an ID (minecraft:zombie, create:andesite_alloy) or a tag with # (#minecraft:logs, #forge:ores). With a tag, a "break 20 logs" quest counts the logs from any mod that puts them in that tag.

You don't have to type anything in the editor: the picker on the right has three tabs, Inventory (your items), All (the whole registry, searchable, mods included) and Tags.

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• Up to 6 reward items, each with its amount and NBT (enchantments, potions, mod data). If the amount exceeds a stack, it is split up; whatever doesn't fit in the inventory drops on the ground.
  • Optional experience.
  • You can hide the reward (the player sees ??? until claiming).

docs.title: Milestones (percentage rewards)
docs.text:
A quest can give intermediate rewards when it reaches certain percentages. The final reward is 100%.

  • Up to 6 milestones, with a percentage from 1 to 99, and their own items and experience.
  • The percentage is the average progress of each objective, so all of them weigh the same. In a community quest it uses the global progress.
  • They are claimed with Claim milestone!, without waiting for the quest to be completed. Claiming the final reward also hands out any milestones left.
  • In the editor: Rewards page, the top button switches between the final reward and each milestone (+ creates one, ✕ deletes it).

docs.title: Requirements (chains)
docs.text: A quest can require that others are claimed. Until then it shows as Locked and you can see what is missing. Cycles are not allowed.

docs.title: Where it is offered from
docs.text:
Each quest chooses its access:

Access Meaning NPC only Accepted, delivered and claimed with an NPC that offers it Book only Only from the quest book (K key or item), no NPC NPC and book From either

docs.title: Automation
docs.text:
• Auto-accept: accepted as soon as it is unlocked, with no NPC or book. Great for tutorials or advancement-style progressions.
  • Auto-claim: when completed, the rewards go straight to the inventory.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
Sections group quests, for example one per mod. In the panel they appear as a strip of icons on the left, with a green dot if there are rewards to claim and a gold one if there are new quests.

  • Create (admins): the + button of the strip. Right-click a section to edit or delete it (its quests are left without a section).
  • Assign: in the quest editor, General page.
  • NPC by section: in the NPC's Quests tab you can tick whole sections. That NPC offers all their quests, including ones you create later.

docs.title: Community quests
docs.text:
A server-wide counter, and each player decides whether to take part.

  • Joining: the quest appears in Available with the global progress and a Join button. Only what you do after joining counts. Whoever doesn't join neither contributes nor spends items on deliveries.
  • Auto-join (optional): if you prefer an event where everyone is in by default, turn it on in the quest.
  • Claiming: when completed, only those who joined are notified in chat, and those who contributed at least the quest's minimum contribution can claim. Whoever didn't join, or didn't reach the minimum, sees it as closed. Nobody can join after it is completed.
  • Deliveries: delivery objectives work too: what each player hands in adds to the total and to their contribution.
  • Limitations: no requirements and no auto-claim.
  • Repeating an event: /questmod community reset <quest>.

Performance

Community progress is sent to players in batches, at most once per second, so hundreds of kills don't flood the network.

docs.title: Editing and deleting
docs.text: Admins see Edit and Delete (with confirmation) in the panel. Quests that come from a datapack are read-only in game.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: Key Action K Opens the quest book G Shows or hides each quest's steps in the HUD

docs.title: Client configuration
docs.text:
File config/questmod-client.toml.

Option Default Description hud.enabled true Shows the progress of active quests on screen hud.side LEFT HUD side: LEFT or RIGHT hud.maxQuests 5 Maximum quests shown in the HUD (1 to 10) hud.expanded false Shows each quest's steps separately (toggled with the G key) npc.allowUrlSkins true Allows downloading skins from https links set on NPCs by the server npc.showNpcMarker true Shows the ! above NPCs

docs.title: Server configuration
docs.text:
File serverconfig/questmod-server.toml of each world (or defaultconfigs/questmod-server.toml to set values in a modpack).

Option Default Description general.adminPermissionLevel 2 Op level needed to manage quests and NPCs (0 to 4) general.singleplayerOwnerIsAdmin true In a singleplayer world, the owner is an admin even without cheats general.bookEnabled true Enables the quest book (key and item) general.giveBook FIRST_JOIN When the book is given: NEVER, FIRST_JOIN (once per player) or IF_MISSING (on every join, if not carrying one)

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
For admins (the configured level, 2 by default; the console and command blocks use that same level).

Command What it does /questmod export <namespace> Exports the world's quests and sections as a datapack in questmod_export/<namespace>/ /questmod reset <players> [quest] Resets all progress, or a single quest /questmod complete <players> <quest> Marks a quest as completed /questmod community reset <quest> Resets a community quest for everyone (counter, contributions and claimed rewards)

Use the usual /reload to reload datapack quests.

docs.title: Theming
docs.text:
The whole look of the screens and the HUD comes from a normal resource, assets/questmod/theme.json. Any resource pack (including the server's) can override it, and you only need to put the keys you want to change: packs stack and anything missing uses the default theme. It reloads with F3 + T.

Example pack

In the repository, docs/ejemplo_tema/ is a complete resource pack (wood and gold) with textures ready to copy and modify.

docs.title: Colors and sizes
docs.text:
colors uses RRGGBB (opaque) or AARRGGBB. layout holds sizes in pixels (panel_width, list_width, hud_max_width...). The keys and their defaults are in the Reference.

{
  "colors": { "title": "55FFFF", "btn_accept": "AA00AA", "panel": "F00A0A2A" },
  "layout": { "panel_width": 420 }
}

docs.title: Textures (skins)
docs.text:
Each element can have an optional texture. If it has none, it is drawn with its usual color.

"skins": {
  "button": {
    "texture": "mypack:textures/gui/button.png",
    "width": 24, "height": 20,
    "border": 3,
    "hover":    { "v": 20 },
    "disabled": { "v": 40 }
  }
}
Field Description texture The image. The only required field (its size is detected automatically) u, v, width, height Which part of the image to use (default, all of it). Lets you put several states in one sheet border Border thickness for 9-slice: corners aren't distorted and the rest stretches, so one small PNG works at any size hover, disabled, selected State variants. They inherit the skin and only change what you specify (almost always v)

Setting "key": null removes the texture set by an earlier pack.

Tips

  • Keep textures small and use border so they scale well.
  • A sheet with the three states stacked (normal, hover, disabled) is declared with "hover": {"v": 20}, "disabled": {"v": 40}.
  • The status color stripe of the rows is adjusted with layout.entry_stripe (0 hides it).
  • A broken skin (missing image, bad JSON) breaks nothing: it is reported in the log and the color is used.

docs.title: Section icons as images
docs.text: A section's icon can be an image instead of an item: type the PNG path (mypack:textures/gui/section/create.png) in the icon field. It is scaled to 16×16.
